_doc: BINANCE-AGENT-OS-GEO-AND-SUBMISSIONS-W2 CH1 R4 — the declaration read by scripts/check-rendered-comment-hygiene.mjs. A developer note written as an <!-- --> comment inside a generator's template literal is PUBLIC COPY: it ships to View Source on every page that generator emits. Measured 2026-08-26, before this wave: 8 flavoured comments on each of 25 rendered integration pages, one of them quoting an internal directive by name. The gate is ALLOW-LIST shaped — a deny-list of internal tokens is one new wave-ID format away from silence.
_severity_doc: TWO severities, because the gate cannot be CLEAN over the whole tree on day one and a gate that blocks on 42 pre-existing leaks would simply be disabled. BLOCK covers the surface this wave owns and cleaned; REPORT covers everything else, behind a promotion criterion that carries BOTH a count and a DEADLINE. A guard permanently stuck in REPORT is decoration (git-and-worktrees.md:17), so every run appends its count and the healing RATE is measured at the decision rather than guessed.
_blocking_globs_reason: The 25 pages CH1 re-renders from scripts/render-integrations.mjs, whose template this wave cleaned. Every leak here is one this wave is responsible for, so blocking costs nothing and prevents regression.
_report_globs_reason: Everything else under landing/. These files are emitted by build_nav.mjs, build_docs.mjs, build_landing.mjs, render-jsx-static.mjs, build_channel_pages.mjs and build_tools_page.mjs — cleaning them is a multi-generator public-copy sweep, a different risk class from this chapter, and CH1's Must-NOT-write forbids those generators outright.

allowed_markers.reason: Nav injection region. scripts/build_nav.mjs replaces the content between these two markers; they are load-bearing and must survive byte-identical.
Analytics snippet region injected by scripts/build_analytics.mjs. Same contract as NAV.
Generated-block markers consumed by scripts/build_landing.mjs and scripts/build_docs.mjs (BUILD:connect-exchange-kit, BUILD:INTEGRATIONS_INDEX_*, and the slash-closed llms.txt form).

Canonical design-loader boundary emitted by four generators. W2 CH1 stripped its '(DESIGN-W2 / D2-C)' parenthetical from render-integrations.mjs — the wave ID was decoration, the marker text is the contract.
Marks a line auto-injected from the live SoT by scripts/snapshot-landing-data.mjs. Hand-editing a marked line breaks the injector.
Template placeholder in landing/_templates/*.template.html, substituted at generation time.

Snapshot-provenance marker carried from the tutorial markdown. render-integrations.mjs's stripSnapshotBlock() matches on it, so it is functional, not prose. The dash character varies by upstream source (em dash, en dash, double hyphen), hence the character class.
Fixed label emitted inside the analytics region by build_analytics.mjs. Carries no internal identifier and is part of that generator's stable output.

promotion.criterion: report_lane_leaks == 0 AND every remaining comment in the report globs matches allowed_markers
promotion._decide_by_reason: A DEADLINE, not a waiting period. The count alone can never fire if the report lane does not heal, and nothing schedules it to heal — the six generators that emit these comments are untouched by this wave. On this date somebody DECIDES: promote, extend with a stated reason, or delete the report lane as decoration.

observed.note: Baseline recorded by the wave's first live run; see the run output appended below. Before CH1 the BLOCKING surface carried 8 flavoured comments on each of 25 pages; after CH1 it carries zero.

promotion._observed_doc: Append one row per decision-point run so the healing RATE is measurable rather than guessed. A flat count with no series cannot distinguish 'slowly healing' from 'structurally stuck'.

instrument.population: Non-conforming HTML comments in the REPORT globs — every <!-- --> in landing/**/*.html outside landing/integrations/ that matches no allowed_markers row. Counted live per run.
instrument.written_by: scripts/check-rendered-comment-hygiene.mjs — the subject of this criterion. It READS the committed tree and writes none of it.
instrument.rederive: Re-derive at any commit without trusting a recorded number: `git checkout <sha> && node scripts/check-rendered-comment-hygiene.mjs` and read the REPORT-lane count. The population is the committed HTML corpus, which git preserves, so a past value is recomputable rather than merely remembered — and the gate cannot inflate or deflate it, because it only reads files that six OTHER generators write.
instrument.reason: B, not C: the gate is the instrument, but a deliberate invocation cannot MANUFACTURE the value — the count is a pure function of the committed tree, and lowering it requires actually editing one of the 16 files. B, not D: unlike a live-world observation, every past sample is recomputable from git at the corresponding SHA, so observed[] is a convenience rather than the only record. B, not A: the producer and the subject are the same script, so the independence comes from re-derivability, not from a separate population.
